 사진 확대 President Lee Jae Myung is holding a meeting with reporters in the lobby of the Blue House's Chunchugwan, a press space for journalists on the 19th. [Yonhap News] On the 19th, President Lee Jae Myung approved the appointment of two directors of the Korea Broadcasting Corporation (KBS), which was recommended by the Korea Media and Communications Commission.
 President Lee has approved the appointment of a person to be appointed, presidential spokesman Kang Yoo-jung said in a media announcement.
 Lee Kang-deok, chairman of the Guan Hoon Club's Spiritual Young Fund, and Jang Han-sik, former president of KBS Business, are all recommended for the people's power.
 The Korea Communications Commission held a general meeting on the 15th and recommended President Lee to appoint the two as new directors of KBS.
 Under the revised Broadcasting Act, KBS' board of directors consists of a total of 15 members, including the chairman.
 The recommendation rights are shared by six members of the National Assembly's negotiating group, two by the viewers' committee, three by KBS executives and employees, two by broadcast media-related academic societies, and two by a lawyer's group.
 KBS is currently in the process of appointing its next president.
